items.q: 親の無関心（ ）に、子どもが非行に走る場合がある。
items.qr: Oya no mukanshin (___) ni, kodomo ga hikou ni hashiru baai ga aru.
items.en: Sometimes, because of parents' lack of interest, children turn to delinquency.
items.hi: कभी-कभी माता-पिता की उदासीनता के कारण बच्चे ग़लत रास्ते पर चले जाते हैं।
items.gu: ક્યારેક માતા-પિતાની ઉદાસીનતાને કારણે બાળકો ખોટા રસ્તે ચડી જાય છે.
items.why: The blank is followed by に, so we need a word that makes 〜に: ゆえに. せいで already contains で, and せいでに is impossible. のかたわら needs a verb or an activity noun (仕事のかたわら), not 無関心. ならでは is followed by の (日本ならではの), not に.

items.q: 教師と（ ）、すべてを把握しているわけではない。
items.qr: Kyoushi to (___), subete o haaku shite iru wake de wa nai.
items.en: Even a teacher does not know everything.
items.hi: भले ही कोई शिक्षक हो, उसे सब कुछ पता हो, ऐसा नहीं है।
items.gu: ભલે કોઈ શિક્ષક હોય, તેને બધું ખબર હોય એવું નથી.
items.why: "Teacher" is a role you expect to know everything, and the second half denies it (わけではない). That is the concession Nといえども. と＋いうなら would mean "if you call them teachers"; と＋いったから is "because I said"; と＋いうなり is "the moment (he) said". None of them gives "even".

items.q: 今夜ここを出発する（ ）、あさっての朝には着くだろう。
items.qr: Kon'ya koko o shuppatsu suru (___), asatte no asa ni wa tsuku darou.
items.en: If we leave here tonight, we should arrive by the morning of the day after tomorrow.
items.hi: अगर हम आज रात यहाँ से निकलें, तो परसों सुबह तक पहुँच जाएँगे।
items.gu: જો આપણે આજે રાત્રે અહીંથી નીકળીએ, તો પરમ દિવસે સવાર સુધીમાં પહોંચી જઈશું.
items.why: The sentence is a supposition (if we leave tonight) and an estimate (〜だろう). That is とすれば. ともなると／ともなれば attach to nouns of rank, age or time (社長ともなると) and mean "at that level, naturally…". とくれば links two things that go together (夏とくればビール).

items.q: この料理は味（ ）見た目も今一つだ。
items.qr: Kono ryouri wa aji (___) mitame mo imahitotsu da.
items.en: This dish is not great — not only the taste but also the look.
items.hi: यह व्यंजन न सिर्फ़ स्वाद में, बल्कि देखने में भी कुछ ख़ास नहीं है।
items.gu: આ વાનગી માત્ર સ્વાદમાં જ નહીં, દેખાવમાં પણ ખાસ નથી.
items.why: 見た目も tells you that taste is also bad: "not only A but B too". That is AのみならずBも. のみで and だけで mean "only by A" and would need a result like 決まる. 味でなく means "not the taste (but the look)", which contradicts も.

items.q: 私は大学で英語を教える（ ）小説を書いている。
items.qr: Watashi wa daigaku de eigo o oshieru (___) shousetsu o kaite iru.
items.en: While teaching English at a university, I also write novels.
items.hi: मैं विश्वविद्यालय में अंग्रेज़ी पढ़ाने के साथ-साथ उपन्यास भी लिखता हूँ।
items.gu: હું યુનિવર્સિટીમાં અંગ્રેજી ભણાવવાની સાથે સાથે નવલકથાઓ પણ લખું છું.

opts.en: while (on the way), at the same time

items.why: Teaching is the main job, writing novels is a long-term side activity: Vかたわら. がてら is for a short trip that serves two purposes (散歩がてら) and attaches to a noun or V-stem, not 教える. くわえて and ひきかえ need に before them (〜にくわえて, 〜にひきかえ).

items.q: 公園で子どもたちは全身泥（ ）になって遊んでいる。
items.qr: Kouen de kodomotachi wa zenshin doro (___) ni natte asonde iru.
items.en: In the park, the children are playing, covered in mud from head to toe.
items.hi: पार्क में बच्चे सिर से पाँव तक कीचड़ में सने खेल रहे हैं।
items.gu: પાર્કમાં બાળકો માથાથી પગ સુધી કાદવથી ખરડાઈને રમી રહ્યાં છે.
items.why: Mud sticks to the whole body (全身): 泥まみれ. ずくめ means everything is the same thing (黒ずくめの服, いいことずくめ), not dirt on a surface. づくし lists a full set of good things (料理づくし). よごれ is a noun; 泥よごれ is "a mud stain", which cannot describe 全身 here with になって.

items.q: この服はデザイン（ ）古いが、着やすくてもう10年も着ている。
items.qr: Kono fuku wa dezain (___) furui ga, kiyasukute mou juu-nen mo kite iru.
items.en: This outfit's design may be old, but it's comfortable, and I've already worn it for ten years.
items.hi: इस कपड़े का डिज़ाइन भले पुराना है, पर पहनने में आरामदायक है, और मैं इसे दस साल से पहन रहा हूँ।
items.gu: આ કપડાંની ડિઝાઇન ભલે જૂની છે, પણ પહેરવામાં આરામદાયક છે, અને હું તેને દસ વર્ષથી પહેરું છું.
items.why: The sentence admits one weak point (old design) and then praises the clothes (easy to wear, ten years). AこそXが、Y is exactly this concession frame. すら would be "even the design is old", stressing something extreme, not a concession. ゆえ ("because of the design, it is old") makes no sense.

items.q: 昨日、メールを（ ）しました。
items.qr: Kinou, meeru o (___) shimashita.
items.en: I received your email yesterday.
items.hi: मुझे कल आपका ईमेल प्राप्त हुआ।
items.gu: મને ગઈકાલે તમારો ઈમેલ મળ્યો.
items.why: All four are humble 拝〜 verbs, so decide by meaning: what do you do with an email? You receive it: 拝受. 拝借 is for borrowing (お手洗いを拝借), 拝顔 for meeting a superior (拝顔の栄), 拝聴 for listening to a talk.

items.q: 貴社のご返答の（ ）では、弊社は契約解除を求めざるをえません。
items.qr: Kisha no go-hentou no (___) de wa, heisha wa keiyaku kaijo o motomezaru o emasen.
items.en: Depending on your company's reply, we may have no choice but to request cancellation of the contract.
items.hi: आपकी कंपनी के जवाब पर निर्भर करते हुए, हमें अनुबंध रद्द करने की माँग करनी पड़ सकती है।
items.gu: આપની કંપનીના જવાબ પર આધાર રાખીને, અમારે કરાર રદ કરવાની માગણી કરવી પડી શકે.
items.why: The frame N の（ ）では needs a noun, and the meaning is "depending on your reply": いかん. いよいよ and いずれ are adverbs and cannot sit between の and では. いかんせん is also an adverb ("regrettably") that starts a clause.

items.q: 結婚後、弟は以前（ ）、仕事に精を出している。
items.qr: Kekkon go, otouto wa izen (___), shigoto ni sei o dashite iru.
items.en: Since getting married, my younger brother has been working even harder than before.
items.hi: शादी के बाद मेरा छोटा भाई पहले से भी ज़्यादा मेहनत से काम कर रहा है।
items.gu: લગ્ન પછી મારો નાનો ભાઈ પહેલાં કરતાં પણ વધુ મહેનતથી કામ કરે છે.
items.why: 結婚後 contrasts "after marriage" with "before": he works harder than before. 以前にもまして is the set phrase. 以前からずっと would mean he has always worked hard, losing the change that 結婚後 points to. をよそに needs something to ignore (親の心配をよそに). であるものの is a concession and leaves 以前 hanging.

items.q: 部長のご指導（ ）、今回の昇進はありえませんでした。
items.qr: Buchou no go-shidou (___), konkai no shoushin wa ariemasen deshita.
items.en: Without your guidance, sir, this promotion would never have happened.
items.hi: आपके मार्गदर्शन के बिना, यह पदोन्नति संभव नहीं होती।
items.gu: આપના માર્ગદર્શન વિના, આ બઢતી શક્ય ન બનત.
items.why: The ending ありえませんでした ("was impossible") pairs with Nなくしては: "without N, Y could not have happened". The other three would need a verb or adjective before ない (ご指導がないので), and none gives the thank-you logic of the sentence.

items.q: 私の部屋は散らかし（ ）なので、いつも母に怒られる。
items.qr: Watashi no heya wa chirakashi (___) na node, itsumo haha ni okorareru.
items.en: I always leave my room in a mess, so my mother is always scolding me.
items.hi: मैं अपना कमरा हमेशा बिखरा हुआ छोड़ देता हूँ, इसलिए माँ से डाँट पड़ती रहती है।
items.gu: હું મારો રૂમ હંમેશાં અસ્તવ્યસ્ત છોડી દઉં છું, એટલે મમ્મી હંમેશાં ગુસ્સે થાય છે.
items.why: 散らかしたまま片づけない: "messed up and left that way". That is V-stem＋っぱなし, and it takes な before ので (〜っぱなしなので). っぽい is an い-adjective, so 散らかしっぽいので would need no な, and the meaning "tends to scatter" is odd. っぷり (飲みっぷり) describes a style of doing something. っぺ is not a suffix here.

items.q: 日本の夏（ ）蒸し暑くてたまらない。
items.qr: Nihon no natsu (___) mushiatsukute tamaranai.
items.en: Japanese summers are just unbearably hot and humid.
items.hi: जापान की गर्मी की तो बात ही मत करो, इतनी उमस है कि सहन नहीं होती।
items.gu: જાપાનના ઉનાળાની તો વાત જ ન કરો, એટલો બફારો છે કે સહન નથી થતો.

opts.hi: ... की तो बात ही मत करो
opts.gu: ... ની તો વાત જ ન કરો

items.why: 〜てたまらない is a complaint, and ときたら introduces a topic the speaker wants to complain about. によると needs a source (天気予報によると). にすれば needs a person whose view it is (子どもにすれば). とすれば needs a clause or だ (夏だとすれば).

items.q: 携帯電話で話しながら自転車をこぐなんて危険（ ）行為だ。
items.qr: Keitai denwa de hanashinagara jitensha o kogu nante kiken (___) koui da.
items.en: Riding a bicycle while talking on a mobile phone is extremely dangerous.
items.hi: मोबाइल पर बात करते हुए साइकिल चलाना बेहद ख़तरनाक काम है।
items.gu: મોબાઇલ પર વાત કરતાં કરતાં સાઇકલ ચલાવવી અત્યંત જોખમી કામ છે.
items.why: 危険＋きわまりない = "dangerous in the extreme". The other three look alike: きわだつ means "stand out" (きわだった才能) and does not follow 危険. きわどい is itself an adjective ("risky") and cannot be added to 危険. きわまらない is the trap: it seems like the logical negative, but the fixed form is きわまりない (or きわまる).

items.q: 運動不足が体に悪影響を与えることは、言う（ ）。
items.qr: Undou busoku ga karada ni akueikyou o ataeru koto wa, iu (___).
items.en: It goes without saying that lack of exercise has a bad effect on the body.
items.hi: यह कहने की ज़रूरत नहीं कि व्यायाम की कमी शरीर पर बुरा असर डालती है।
items.gu: કહેવાની જરૂર નથી કે કસરતનો અભાવ શરીર પર ખરાબ અસર કરે છે.
items.why: The fact (exercise matters) is obvious, so "there is no need to say it": 言うまでもない. 言うにたえない is not a phrase (聞くにたえない "unbearable to listen to" is). 言うにかぎる ("saying is best") and 言うばかりだ ("just keeps saying") do not match 〜ことは.

items.q: 夏休みの旅行は嫌な ＿＿＿ ＿＿＿ ★ ＿＿＿ だった。
items.qr: Natsuyasumi no ryokou wa iya na ___ ___ ★ ___ datta.
items.en: The summer trip had nothing bad at all — it was nothing but good things.
items.hi: गर्मी की छुट्टियों की यात्रा में एक भी बुरी बात नहीं हुई, सब कुछ अच्छा ही अच्छा था।
items.gu: ઉનાળાની રજાની મુસાફરીમાં એક પણ ખરાબ વાત ન થઈ, બધું સારું જ સારું હતું.
items.why: ★ = 1 (別冊 解答 p.2). Full order 2 → 4 → 1 → 3 (worked out by us; the key gives only the ★ number). ① 嫌な needs a noun: 嫌なことが. ② ことが is the subject of 一つもなく ("there was not one bad thing"). ③ ずくめ needs a noun before it and goes before だった: いいことずくめだった. So the order is ことが → 一つもなく → いいこと → ずくめ, and ★ (3rd slot) is 1 いいこと.

items.q: ＿＿＿ ＿＿＿ ★ ＿＿＿ とは、授業に出席する資格がない。
items.qr: ___ ___ ★ ___ to wa, jugyou ni shusseki suru shikaku ga nai.
items.en: Not even doing your homework, let alone preparing for class — you have no right to attend the lesson.
items.hi: पहले से तैयारी तो दूर, होमवर्क तक नहीं किया — तुम्हें कक्षा में बैठने का हक़ नहीं है।
items.gu: પહેલેથી તૈયારી તો દૂર, હોમવર્ક સુધ્ધાં નથી કર્યું — તને વર્ગમાં બેસવાનો હક નથી.
items.why: ★ = 3 (別冊 解答 p.2). Full order 4 → 1 → 3 → 2 (worked out by us; the key gives only the ★ number). ① おろか needs N は before it: 予習はおろか. ② The pattern continues with N も: 宿題も. ③ していない comes last, before とは. Order 予習は → おろか → 宿題も → していない; ★ (3rd slot) is 3 宿題も. Homework is the more basic task, so it takes も.

items.q: ＿＿＿ ★ ＿＿＿ ＿＿＿ 私は進学することに決めた。
items.qr: ___ ★ ___ ___ watashi wa shingaku suru koto ni kimeta.
items.en: Whether my parents agree or not, I have decided to go on to further study.
items.hi: माता-पिता सहमत हों या न हों, मैंने आगे पढ़ने का फ़ैसला कर लिया है।
items.gu: માતા-પિતા સહમત થાય કે ન થાય, મેં આગળ ભણવાનું નક્કી કરી લીધું છે.
items.why: ★ = 4 (別冊 解答 p.2). Full order 3 → 4 → 2 → 1 (worked out by us; the key gives only the ★ number). ① The pair is fixed: しようが comes before するまいが. ② 賛成 must join する: 賛成しようが. ③ 両親が is the subject of 賛成する and opens the sentence. Order 両親が → 賛成 → しようが → するまいが; ★ (2nd slot) is 4 賛成.

items.q: 皆様のおかげで、留学生活を ＿＿＿ ＿＿＿ ★ ＿＿＿ でした。
items.qr: Minasama no okage de, ryuugaku seikatsu o ___ ___ ★ ___ deshita.
items.en: Thanks to all of you, being able to finish my study abroad safely was the greatest happiness.
items.hi: आप सबकी बदौलत विदेश में पढ़ाई सकुशल पूरी कर पाना मेरे लिए सबसे बड़ी ख़ुशी थी।
items.gu: આપ સૌના કારણે વિદેશમાં અભ્યાસ સહીસલામત પૂરો કરી શક્યો, એ મારા માટે સૌથી મોટી ખુશી હતી.
items.why: ★ = 4 (別冊 解答 p.2). Full order 2 → 1 → 4 → 3 (worked out by us; the key gives only the ★ number). ① 留学生活を needs a verb: 終えられた, with the adverb 無事に in front: 無事に終えられたことは. ② この上ない modifies a noun: この上ない幸せ, which goes before でした. Order 無事に → 終えられたことは → この上ない → 幸せ; ★ (3rd slot) is 4 この上ない.

items.q: 異常気象のせいか、＿＿＿ ★ ＿＿＿ ＿＿＿ 暑い日々が続いている。
items.qr: Ijou kishou no sei ka, ___ ★ ___ ___ atsui hibi ga tsuzuite iru.
items.en: Perhaps because of the strange weather, it has been hot like summer day after day, even though it is spring.
items.hi: शायद असामान्य मौसम की वजह से, वसंत होते हुए भी गर्मियों जैसे गरम दिन चल रहे हैं।
items.gu: કદાચ અસામાન્ય હવામાનને કારણે, વસંત હોવા છતાં ઉનાળા જેવા ગરમ દિવસો ચાલે છે.
items.why: ★ = 4 (別冊 解答 p.2). Full order 1 → 4 → 2 → 3 (worked out by us; the key gives only the ★ number). ① のごとく must sit right before 暑い ("hot like ~"), so it takes the 4th slot. ② Which season is it "like"? Summer: 夏のごとく暑い. ③ なのに follows a noun: 春なのに ("even though it is spring"). Order 春 → なのに → 夏 → のごとく; ★ (2nd slot) is 4 なのに. 夏なのに春のごとく暑い would make no sense.

items.q: 田中さんにとって仕事とは、＿＿＿ ＿＿＿ ★ ＿＿＿ の行為であった。
items.qr: Tanaka-san ni totte shigoto to wa, ___ ___ ★ ___ no koui de atta.
items.en: For Mr Tanaka, work was simply an act for earning his living costs.
items.hi: तनाका-सान के लिए काम बस रोज़ी-रोटी कमाने का ज़रिया था।
items.gu: તનાકા-સાન માટે કામ ફક્ત રોજીરોટી કમાવાનું સાધન હતું.
items.why: ★ = 3 (別冊 解答 p.2). Full order 4 → 1 → 3 → 2 (worked out by us; the key gives only the ★ number). ① ため comes right before の行為: ための行為. ② ため needs a verb in 辞書形 before it: 稼ぐため. ③ 稼ぐ needs an object: 生活費を稼ぐ. ④ ただ limits the whole phrase, so it goes first. Order ただ → 生活費を → 稼ぐ → ため; ★ (3rd slot) is 3 稼ぐ.

items.qr: Kore wa ___ ___ ★ ___ douzou desu.
items.en: This is a bronze statue built to mark the 100th anniversary of the founding.
items.hi: यह स्थापना की 100वीं वर्षगाँठ के उपलक्ष्य में बनाई गई काँसे की मूर्ति है।
items.gu: આ સ્થાપનાની 100મી વર્ષગાંઠના ઉપલક્ષ્યમાં બનાવાયેલી કાંસાની પ્રતિમા છે.
items.why: ★ = 2 (別冊 解答 p.2). Full order 4 → 1 → 2 → 3 (worked out by us; the key gives only the ★ number). ① 建てられた modifies 銅像, so it is last. ② N を記念して: 100周年を記念して. ③ 創立 tells whose anniversary it is and goes before 100周年. Order 創立 → 100周年を → 記念して → 建てられた; ★ (3rd slot) is 2 記念して.

items.q: しかし、現実には年相応の振る舞いは、かならず［１］から傑作なのである。
items.qr: Shikashi, genjitsu ni wa toshisouou no furumai wa, kanarazu [1] kara kessaku na no de aru.
items.en: But in reality, behaviour that fits one's age always comes late, which is why it is so comical.
items.hi: लेकिन असल में उम्र के हिसाब का बर्ताव हमेशा देर से आता है, इसलिए यह मज़ेदार (हास्यास्पद) है।
items.gu: પણ વાસ્તવમાં ઉંમર પ્રમાણેનું વર્તન હંમેશાં મોડું આવે છે, એટલે તે મજેદાર (હાસ્યાસ્પદ) છે.

opts.hi: हर व्यक्ति में अलग होता है
एक ही समय पर आता है

items.why: The next paragraph says 40-year-old behaviour is never seen at 35 and people regret it only years after 40, and the passage later repeats 年相応の振る舞いが遅れてしまう. So the blank is 遅れてしまう. かならず ("always") rules out 1 (it does not vary by person). 3 is the opposite. 傑作 here is ironic: "comical, a joke".

items.q: いつでも四十歳を過ぎて何年かしてから、「しまった。もっと年相応に振る舞うべきだった」と、［２］。
items.qr: Itsu demo yonjussai o sugite nannen ka shite kara, "Shimatta. Motto toshisouou ni furumau beki datta" to, [2].
items.en: It is always several years after turning forty that people regret it: "Oh no, I should have acted my age."
items.hi: हमेशा चालीस पार करने के कुछ साल बाद ही इंसान पछताता है: "अरे! मुझे उम्र के हिसाब से बर्ताव करना चाहिए था।"
items.gu: હંમેશાં ચાળીસ વટાવ્યા પછી થોડાં વર્ષે જ માણસ પસ્તાય છે: "અરે! મારે ઉંમર પ્રમાણે વર્તવું જોઈતું હતું."

opts.t: 後悔するつもりである

items.why: いつでも ("always") shows a general truth, so the verb is non-past with explanatory のである: 後悔するのである. 1 is past, for one event. 2 gives advice, which the writer is not doing here. 4 (intend to regret) is illogical.

items.q: ［３］、年相応に振る舞うのが遅れてしまうのだろうか。
items.qr: [3], toshisouou ni furumau no ga okurete shimau no darou ka.
items.en: Why is it that we are late in acting our age?
items.hi: ऐसा क्यों होता है कि उम्र के हिसाब से बर्ताव करने में हम देर कर देते हैं?
items.gu: આવું કેમ થાય છે કે ઉંમર પ્રમાણે વર્તવામાં આપણે મોડા પડીએ છીએ?
items.why: The sentence ends with 〜のだろうか, a question, and the following sentences answer it with 〜からだ ("it is because…") twice. So the question word なぜ is needed. The other three are connectors for statements.

items.q: 人間は日々年々、自分は何歳であると自覚して年をとっていく［４］。
items.qr: Ningen wa hibi toshidoshi, jibun wa nansai de aru to jikaku shite toshi o totte iku [4].
items.en: It is not the case that people grow older day by day, year by year, always aware of how old they are.
items.hi: ऐसा नहीं है कि इंसान हर दिन, हर साल यह जानते हुए बूढ़ा होता है कि वह कितने साल का है।
items.gu: એવું નથી કે માણસ દરરોજ, દર વર્ષે એ જાણીને મોટો થાય છે કે પોતે કેટલા વર્ષનો છે.

opts.en: that is why, so it is
it is not the case that ✓

items.why: The next sentence says most people think of themselves as younger than they really are. That only follows if this sentence denies that people track their age: わけではない. わけである would agree with the idea. わけない means "easy", and わけがある means "there is a reason", neither of which fits.

items.q: しかし、年をとり年齢にふさわしい行動や考えができないと、［５-a］、［５-b］を晒すことになる。
items.qr: Shikashi, toshi o tori nenrei ni fusawashii koudou ya kangae ga dekinai to, [5-a], [5-b] o sarasu koto ni naru.
items.en: But if, as you grow older, you cannot act and think in a way that fits your age, you end up exposing an ugly figure and an ugly attitude.
items.hi: लेकिन अगर उम्र बढ़ने पर भी उसके अनुरूप व्यवहार और सोच न हो, तो इंसान अपना भद्दा रूप और भद्दा रवैया उजागर कर बैठता है।
items.gu: પણ જો ઉંમર વધવા છતાં તેને અનુરૂપ વર્તન અને વિચાર ન આવે, તો માણસ પોતાનું ભદ્દું રૂપ અને ભદ્દું વલણ ઉઘાડું પાડી બેસે છે.

opts.t: a 美しい姿 ／ b 美しい態度
opts.r: a utsukushii sugata / b utsukushii taido
opts.en: a beautiful figure / a beautiful attitude

opts.t: a 美しい姿 ／ b 醜い態度
opts.r: a utsukushii sugata / b minikui taido
opts.en: a beautiful figure / an ugly attitude

opts.t: a 醜い姿 ／ b 醜い態度
opts.r: a minikui sugata / b minikui taido
opts.en: an ugly figure / an ugly attitude ✓

opts.t: a 醜い姿 ／ b 美しい態度
opts.r: a minikui sugata / b utsukushii taido
opts.en: an ugly figure / a beautiful attitude

items.why: The condition 〜ができないと is negative, so the result is negative too, and 晒す ("expose to view") usually takes something shameful: 恥を晒す, 醜態を晒す. Both a and b are listed side by side (、) as the same kind of thing, so both must be 醜い. Mixed pairs (2, 4) break the parallel; 1 is the opposite meaning.

items.q: 台風のせいで電車が止まらない（ ）から、今日は出かけるのはやめよう。
items.qr: Taifuu no sei de densha ga tomaranai (___) kara, kyou wa dekakeru no wa yameyou.
items.en: The trains might stop because of the typhoon, so let's not go out today.
items.hi: तूफ़ान की वजह से ट्रेनें रुक भी सकती हैं, इसलिए आज बाहर नहीं जाते।
items.gu: વાવાઝોડાને લીધે ટ્રેનો બંધ પણ થઈ શકે, એટલે આજે બહાર નથી જતા.

opts.hi: यह भी कहा जा सकता है

items.why: The decision (出かけるのはやめよう) needs a risk as its reason: 止まらないともかぎらない = "they might stop". With 3 or 4 the sentence would claim "it can be said that the trains won't stop", which is no reason to stay home. 2 is not a grammar pattern.
items.unit: まとめ 文法 問題1–3

items.q: 「お疲れ様」という言葉は、先生に使え（ ）が、使わないほうがいい。
items.qr: "Otsukaresama" to iu kotoba wa, sensei ni tsukae (___) ga, tsukawanai hou ga ii.
items.en: You can use the word otsukaresama to a teacher, but it is better not to.
items.hi: "ओत्सुकारेसामा" शब्द शिक्षक से इस्तेमाल तो कर सकते हैं, पर न करना बेहतर है।
items.gu: "ઓત્સુકારેસામા" શબ્દ શિક્ષક સામે વાપરી તો શકાય, પણ ન વાપરવો સારું.

opts.hi: ऐसा नहीं कि नहीं कर सकते

items.why: 〜が、使わないほうがいい needs "possible, but better not". 1 gives "can't, but better not" — no contrast. 3 says "just use it", which contradicts the advice; 4 is a past regret. Only 使えなくはない is a weak "yes" that can be followed by が.
items.unit: まとめ 文法 問題1–3

items.q: 吉田さんにマイクを（ ）、マイクを一人占めしてしまうだろう。
items.qr: Yoshida-san ni maiku o (___), maiku o hitorijime shite shimau darou.
items.en: If you ever hand Yoshida-san the mic, he'll keep it all to himself.
items.hi: अगर योशिदा-सान को माइक दे दिया, तो वह उसे अकेले ही पकड़े रहेंगे।
items.gu: જો યોશિદા-સાનને માઇક આપી દીધું, તો તે એકલા જ પકડી રાખશે.
items.why: The "terrible result" pattern is V-意向形＋ものなら (渡そう). The past and dictionary forms (2, 3) are not used with ものなら in this meaning. 4 uses the intransitive 渡る, which cannot take マイクを.
items.unit: まとめ 文法 問題1–3

items.q: 一人暮らしを始めてから（ ）、野菜を食べていない。
items.qr: Hitorigurashi o hajimete kara (___), yasai o tabete inai.
items.en: Ever since I started living alone, I haven't eaten vegetables.
items.hi: जब से अकेले रहना शुरू किया है, तब से सब्ज़ियाँ नहीं खाईं।
items.gu: જ્યારથી એકલો રહેવા લાગ્યો છું, ત્યારથી શાકભાજી નથી ખાધી.

opts.hi: कहने पर, की बात हो तो
opts.gu: કહીએ તો, ની વાત થાય તો

items.why: 〜てから＋というもの = "ever since", and the continuing negative (食べていない) confirms a long state. とはいえ needs a contrast ("I started living alone; even so…"), and といえば／というと introduce a topic, not a time span.
items.unit: まとめ 文法 問題1–3

items.q: テストも終わった（ ）、今夜はみんなで飲みに行こう。
items.qr: Tesuto mo owatta (___), kon'ya wa minna de nomi ni ikou.
items.en: The test is over now, so let's all go out for drinks tonight.
items.hi: परीक्षा भी ख़त्म हो गई है, तो आज रात सब पीने चलते हैं।
items.gu: પરીક્ષા પણ પૂરી થઈ ગઈ છે, તો આજે રાત્રે બધા પીવા જઈએ.
items.why: An invitation (行こう) after a light reason calls for 〜ことだし. とはいえ gives the wrong logic (contrast). というので reports a reason someone stated and sounds odd before 行こう. ことで states a means or cause of a result, not a reason for a suggestion.
items.unit: まとめ 文法 問題1–3

items.q: 今度のパーティーで ＿＿＿ ＿＿＿ ★ ＿＿＿ もらえませんか。
items.qr: Kondo no paatii de ___ ___ ★ ___ moraemasen ka.
items.en: Could you let him play the guitar at the next party?
items.hi: क्या अगली पार्टी में आप उसे गिटार बजाने देंगे?
items.gu: આવતી પાર્ટીમાં તમે તેને ગિટાર વગાડવા દેશો?
items.why: ★ = 4 (別冊 解答 p.4). Full order 3 → 2 → 4 → 1 (worked out by us; the key gives only the ★ number). ① もらえませんか needs a て-form right before it: やって. ② やって follows the causative: 演奏させてやって. ③ The causative takes 人に and 物を: 彼にギターを演奏させる. ★ (3rd slot) is 4 演奏させて.
items.unit: まとめ 文法 問題1–3

items.q: ＿＿＿ ★ ＿＿＿ ＿＿＿ うそ、すぐに見破られるよ。
items.qr: ___ ★ ___ ___ uso, sugu ni miyaburareru yo.
items.en: You're not a child — a silly lie like that will be seen through at once.
items.hi: तुम कोई बच्चे नहीं हो — ऐसा बेतुका झूठ तुरंत पकड़ा जाएगा।
items.gu: તું કંઈ બાળક નથી — આવું વાહિયાત જૂઠાણું તરત પકડાઈ જશે.
items.why: ★ = 3 (別冊 解答 p.4). Full order 1 → 3 → 4 → 2 (ours). ① N＋じゃあるまいし: 子どもじゃあるまいし. ② The words before うそ describe it: そんなばかばかしいうそ (そんな goes first, then the adjective). ★ (2nd slot) is 3 じゃあるまいし.
items.unit: まとめ 文法 問題1–3

items.q: 彼は ＿＿＿ ＿＿＿ ★ ＿＿＿ と言われている。
items.qr: Kare wa ___ ___ ★ ___ to iwarete iru.
items.en: He is said to have a tendency to blurt out whatever he thinks.
items.hi: कहा जाता है कि उसकी आदत है, जो सोचता है तुरंत बोल देता है।
items.gu: કહેવાય છે કે તેની આદત છે, જે વિચારે તે તરત બોલી દે છે.
items.why: ★ = 2 (別冊 解答 p.4). Full order 4 → 3 → 2 → 1 (ours). ① きらいがある comes last before と言われている and needs a dictionary-form verb: 口にするきらいがある. ② 口にする takes an object with を: 思ったことを口にする. ③ すぐに modifies the verb and sits right before it. ★ (3rd slot) is 2 口にする.
items.unit: まとめ 文法 問題1–3

items.q: ［１］こうした上達能力自体の向上にも上達のプロセスがあるのであって、はじめからあまりに複雑な状況（フィールド）での経験は整理しにくい。
items.qr: [1] kou shita joutatsu nouryoku jitai no koujou ni mo joutatsu no purosesu ga aru no de atte, hajime kara amari ni fukuzatsu na joukyou (fiirudo) de no keiken wa seiri shinikui.
items.en: However, improving this ability itself also has a process, and experience in overly complex situations from the start is hard to sort out.
items.hi: लेकिन इस क्षमता को बढ़ाने की भी एक प्रक्रिया है, और शुरू से ही बहुत उलझी स्थितियों का अनुभव समझना मुश्किल होता है।
items.gu: પરંતુ આ ક્ષમતાને વધારવાની પણ એક પ્રક્રિયા છે, અને શરૂઆતથી જ બહુ જટિલ પરિસ્થિતિઓનો અનુભવ સમજવો અઘરો હોય છે.
items.why: The previous paragraph ends on a hopeful note: the ability can be learned in any field. Blank 1 adds a limitation ("but it also has a process; complex settings are hard at first"), so a contrast connector is needed: しかし. また and さらには only add similar points; その代わり offers a trade-off.
items.unit: まとめ 文法 問題1–3

items.q: その後の複雑な現実における自分の闘い方を見つけていくための、［２］「箱庭的」な世界における上達モデルの獲得が基礎段階としてまず必要なのである。
items.qr: Sono go no fukuzatsu na genjitsu ni okeru jibun no tatakaikata o mitsukete iku tame no, [2] "hakoniwateki" na sekai ni okeru joutatsu moderu no kakutoku ga kiso dankai to shite mazu hitsuyou na no de aru.
items.en: As a first, basic stage, what is needed is to gain a model of improvement in a "miniature-garden", so to speak, world, so that you can later find your own way to fight in complex reality.
items.hi: बाद में उलझी असलियत में अपना लड़ने का तरीका खोजने के लिए, बुनियादी चरण के तौर पर पहले, यूँ कहें तो, एक "छोटी मॉडल दुनिया" में प्रगति का मॉडल पाना ज़रूरी है।
items.gu: પછી જટિલ વાસ્તવિકતામાં પોતાની લડવાની રીત શોધવા માટે, પાયાના તબક્કા તરીકે પહેલાં, કહો કે, એક "નાની મૉડલ દુનિયા"માં પ્રગતિનું મૉડલ મેળવવું જરૂરી છે.
items.why: 「箱庭的」 is in quotation marks because it is a metaphor (a miniature garden for a simplified world). いわば ("so to speak") is the adverb that introduces such a figure of speech. いっそ expresses a drastic choice, いかにも "really looks like", あくまで "strictly / persistently" — none introduces a metaphor.
items.unit: まとめ 文法 問題1–3

items.q: スポーツには明確なルールがあり、現実よりもはるかに条件が［３］。
items.qr: Supootsu ni wa meikaku na ruuru ga ari, genjitsu yori mo haruka ni jouken ga [3].
items.en: Sports have clear rules, and their conditions are far more limited than in reality.
items.hi: खेलों के नियम साफ़ होते हैं, और उनकी शर्तें असल ज़िंदगी से कहीं ज़्यादा सीमित होती हैं।
items.gu: રમતોના નિયમો સ્પષ્ટ હોય છે, અને તેની શરતો વાસ્તવિક જીવન કરતાં ઘણી વધુ મર્યાદિત હોય છે.

opts.gu: ધીમે ધીમે મર્યાદિત થઈ રહી છે

items.why: 条件が is the subject, so the passive is needed (conditions are limited), which rules out 2. The next sentence gives table tennis rules as examples of 限定, so the meaning is positive "limited", not 3. Rules describe a fixed state, so 〜ている fits, not the gradual change of 〜つつある (1).
items.unit: まとめ 文法 問題1–3

items.q: こうした諸限定によって、必要な技が確立［４］。
items.qr: Kou shita sho-gentei ni yotte, hitsuyou na waza ga kakuritsu [4].
items.en: These limits make it easier for the necessary skills to be established.
items.hi: इन सीमाओं की वजह से ज़रूरी कौशल स्थापित होना आसान हो जाता है।
items.gu: આ મર્યાદાઓને લીધે જરૂરી કૌશલ સ્થાપિત થવું સહેલું બને છે.

opts.hi: स्थापित होना आसान हो जाता है

items.why: 〜によって shows the limits cause a result, and the next sentence continues "once the skills are clear, practice methods are devised" — a positive effect. Negative 1 and 3 contradict this, and 4 ("has sometimes happened") is too weak for a general cause–effect claim.
items.unit: まとめ 文法 問題1–3

items.q: 「上達の普遍的な論理」を獲得するという点からいえば、［５-a］が競技力の大半を決定してしまうスポーツよりは、［５-b］が競技力を左右するスポーツのほうが意義が大きい。
items.qr: "Joutatsu no fuhenteki na ronri" o kakutoku suru to iu ten kara ieba, [5-a] ga kyougiryoku no taihan o kettei shite shimau supootsu yori wa, [5-b] ga kyougiryoku o sayuu suru supootsu no hou ga igi ga ookii.
items.en: From the point of view of acquiring "the general logic of improvement", sports in which [b] determines ability are more meaningful than sports in which [a] decides most of one's ability.
items.hi: "प्रगति के सार्वभौमिक तर्क" को पाने की दृष्टि से, जिन खेलों में [a] ज़्यादातर क्षमता तय करता है, उनसे वे खेल ज़्यादा सार्थक हैं जिनमें [b] क्षमता तय करता है।
items.gu: "પ્રગતિના સાર્વત્રિક તર્ક"ને મેળવવાની દૃષ્ટિએ, જે રમતોમાં [a] મોટા ભાગની ક્ષમતા નક્કી કરે છે, તેના કરતાં એવી રમતો વધુ અર્થપૂર્ણ છે જેમાં [b] ક્ષમતા નક્કી કરે છે.

opts.t: a 生来の運動能力やセンス ／ b 人工的な努力の結果
opts.r: a seirai no undou nouryoku ya sensu / b jinkouteki na doryoku no kekka
opts.en: a inborn ability and sense / b the result of artificial effort
opts.hi: a जन्मजात क्षमता / b कृत्रिम प्रयास का परिणाम
opts.gu: a જન્મજાત ક્ષમતા / b કૃત્રિમ પ્રયાસનું પરિણામ

opts.t: a 生来の運動能力やセンス ／ b 練習による技術の習得
opts.r: a seirai no undou nouryoku ya sensu / b renshuu ni yoru gijutsu no shuutoku
opts.en: a inborn ability and sense / b skill acquired by practice ✓
opts.hi: a जन्मजात क्षमता / b अभ्यास से पाया कौशल
opts.gu: a જન્મજાત ક્ષમતા / b અભ્યાસથી મેળવેલું કૌશલ

opts.t: a 練習による技術の習得 ／ b 人工的な努力の結果
opts.r: a renshuu ni yoru gijutsu no shuutoku / b jinkouteki na doryoku no kekka
opts.en: a skill by practice / b result of artificial effort
opts.hi: a अभ्यास से कौशल / b कृत्रिम प्रयास
opts.gu: a અભ્યાસથી કૌશલ / b કૃત્રિમ પ્રયાસ

opts.t: a 練習による技術の習得 ／ b 生来の運動能力やセンス
opts.r: a renshuu ni yoru gijutsu no shuutoku / b seirai no undou nouryoku ya sensu
opts.en: a skill by practice / b inborn ability
opts.hi: a अभ्यास से कौशल / b जन्मजात क्षमता
opts.gu: a અભ્યાસથી કૌશલ / b જન્મજાત ક્ષમતા

items.why: The whole passage praises learning skills (技) through practice, so the "more meaningful" sport (b) must be the one decided by 練習による技術の習得, and the contrast (a) is inborn talent. That leaves 1 or 2. 2 repeats the passage's own words (技術, 練習, 習得); 人工的な努力 ("artificial effort") is never the writer's term and sounds negative. 4 reverses the argument; 3 has no contrast.
items.unit: まとめ 文法 問題1–3

items.q: 快いリズムに合わせて、ダンスを踊り続けた。
items.qr: Kokoroyoi rizumu ni awasete, dansu o odoritsuzuketa.
items.en: We kept dancing to the pleasant rhythm.
items.hi: हम सुखद लय के साथ नाचते रहे।
items.gu: અમે સુખદ લય સાથે નાચતા રહ્યા.

opts.en: fast (a different word, written 速い／早い)
comfortable (a different word, written 心地よい)

items.why: 快い is read こころよい. The big trap is 4: ここちよい means almost the same ("comfortable, pleasant") and would fit the sentence, but it is written 心地よい, not 快い. 1 is a sound guess from 快速 (かいそく, "rapid"); 2 is a real word with no kanji.
items.unit: まとめ 文字・語彙 問題1–4

items.q: 忙しい生活の中で、人間関係が希薄になっているような気がする。
items.qr: Isogashii seikatsu no naka de, ningen kankei ga kihaku ni natte iru you na ki ga suru.
items.en: I feel that in our busy lives, human relationships are becoming thin.
items.hi: मुझे लगता है कि व्यस्त जीवन में इंसानी रिश्ते कमज़ोर होते जा रहे हैं।
items.gu: મને લાગે છે કે વ્યસ્ત જીવનમાં માણસના સંબંધો નબળા પડતા જાય છે.

opts.en: not a reading of 希薄 (思慕 しぼ "longing" is a different word)
scale, size (a different word, written 規模)

items.why: 希 = き (希望 kibou) and 薄 = はく (軽薄 keihaku). The distractors swap in other sounds: し instead of き for the first kanji, and ぼ (as in 規模 きぼ, a real word) instead of はく for the second. 希薄 is a fixed N1 word for weak ties or thin air.
items.unit: まとめ 文字・語彙 問題1–4

items.q: 長旅に出ていたせいか、世事に疎くなっている。
items.qr: Nagatabi ni dete ita sei ka, seji ni utoku natte iru.
items.en: Maybe because I was away on a long trip, I've become out of touch with what's going on in the world.
items.hi: शायद लंबी यात्रा पर रहने की वजह से मैं दुनिया की बातों से बेख़बर हो गया हूँ।
items.gu: કદાચ લાંબી મુસાફરીને લીધે હું દુનિયાની વાતોથી બેખબર થઈ ગયો છું.

opts.en: dull, slow (a different word, written 鈍く)
for a long time (a different word, written 久しく)
opts.hi: लंबे समय से (अलग शब्द, 久しく)

opts.en: filthy, disgusting (a different word, written 汚らわしく)

items.why: 疎い = うとい, and 〜に疎い is a set pattern: "out of touch with / know little about ~" (世事に疎い, 機械に疎い). All three wrong options are real adjectives; 鈍い (にぶい) is the tempting one because its meaning ("slow-witted") is close, but its kanji is 鈍, not 疎.
items.unit: まとめ 文字・語彙 問題1–4

items.q: 社長就任にあたり、将来の（ ）を語った。
items.qr: Shachou shuunin ni atari, shourai no ( ) o katatta.
items.en: On becoming company president, he spoke about his aspirations for the future.
items.hi: अध्यक्ष का पद सँभालते समय उन्होंने भविष्य के अपने संकल्प बताए।
items.gu: પ્રમુખપદ સંભાળતી વખતે તેમણે ભવિષ્યના પોતાના સંકલ્પો કહ્યા.
items.why: 抱負を語る／述べる is the set phrase for stating your plans when starting a new role or year. 初心 looks back to how you felt at the start (初心に返る, 初心を忘れない), so 将来の初心 is odd. 執念 is a dark, obsessive drive (執念を燃やす). 自信 does not pair with 将来の…を語る.
items.unit: まとめ 文字・語彙 問題1–4

items.q: 悩みがあるときには、専門家の（ ）を受けることにしている。
items.qr: Nayami ga aru toki ni wa, senmonka no ( ) o ukeru koto ni shite iru.
items.en: When I have worries, I make a point of getting counselling from a professional.
items.hi: जब मुझे कोई परेशानी होती है, तो मैं विशेषज्ञ से परामर्श लेता हूँ।
items.gu: જ્યારે મને કોઈ મૂંઝવણ હોય, ત્યારે હું નિષ્ણાતનું પરામર્શ લઉં છું.
items.why: 悩み points to counselling: カウンセリングを受ける. オリエンテーション is for new students or staff, カリキュラム is a course plan (you don't 受ける it from an expert), and ガイド is a person or guidebook, not a service for worries.
items.unit: まとめ 文字・語彙 問題1–4

items.q: 日に（ ）、野菜の水分が自然に蒸発するのを待つことにした。
items.qr: Hi ni ( ), yasai no suibun ga shizen ni jouhatsu suru no o matsu koto ni shita.
items.en: I decided to leave the vegetables out in the sun and wait for their moisture to evaporate naturally.
items.hi: मैंने सब्ज़ियों को धूप में खुला रखकर उनकी नमी अपने-आप उड़ने का इंतज़ार करने का फ़ैसला किया।
items.gu: મેં શાકભાજીને તડકામાં ખુલ્લાં રાખીને તેનો ભેજ આપમેળે ઊડી જાય તેની રાહ જોવાનું નક્કી કર્યું.
items.why: The speaker is acting on the vegetables, so we need a transitive verb that takes 日に: 日にさらす "expose to the sun" (also 風にさらす, 危険にさらす). 焼ける and 当たる are intransitive — 日に焼ける is getting a tan; 日に当たる needs the vegetables as subject (日に当てる would be the transitive form). 出す would need 日なたに出して or 外に出して; 日に出す is not used.
items.unit: まとめ 文字・語彙 問題1–4

items.q: 論文作成に思ったより時間がかかり、提出最終日に（ ）間に合った。
items.qr: Ronbun sakusei ni omotta yori jikan ga kakari, teishutsu saishuubi ni ( ) ma ni atta.
items.en: Writing the thesis took longer than I expected, and I only just made it on the last day for submission.
items.hi: शोध-पत्र लिखने में सोच से ज़्यादा समय लगा, और जमा करने के आख़िरी दिन मैं बाल-बाल समय पर पहुँचा।
items.gu: શોધપત્ર લખવામાં ધાર્યા કરતાં વધુ સમય લાગ્યો, અને જમા કરવાના છેલ્લા દિવસે હું માંડ માંડ સમયસર પહોંચ્યો.
items.why: ぎりぎり間に合う "just make it in time" is the fixed collocation, and 思ったより時間がかかり tells us it was close. きっかり and きっちり mean "exactly" (きっかり3時), which does not suit a near miss. きりきり is for pain (胃がきりきり痛む) or busy work (きりきり働く). The voicing き／ぎ is the trap.
items.unit: まとめ 文字・語彙 問題1–4

items.q: 選挙にあたり、候補者は必死の形相で最後まで戦った。
items.qr: Senkyo ni atari, kouhosha wa hisshi no gyousou de saigo made tatakatta.
items.en: In the election, the candidate fought to the end with a desperate look on his face.
items.hi: चुनाव में उम्मीदवार चेहरे पर जी-जान वाला भाव लिए आख़िर तक लड़ा।
items.gu: ચૂંટણીમાં ઉમેદવાર ચહેરા પર જીવ સટોસટનો ભાવ લઈને છેક સુધી લડ્યો.
items.why: 形相 is a (usually intense) facial expression, so it matches 顔つき. 顔立ち is the face you were born with (整った顔立ち), not a passing expression. 体面 and 面目 are "face" in the social sense — honour or reputation (面目を保つ, 体面を気にする) — a trap because of the shared 面.
items.unit: まとめ 文字・語彙 問題1–4

items.q: サボっているところを部長に見られ、彼はそそくさと席に戻った。
items.qr: Sabotte iru tokoro o buchou ni mirare, kare wa sosokusa to seki ni modotta.
items.en: The manager caught him slacking off, and he hurried back to his seat.
items.hi: मैनेजर ने उसे काम से जी चुराते देख लिया, और वह हड़बड़ी में अपनी सीट पर लौट गया।
items.gu: મૅનેજરે તેને કામચોરી કરતો જોઈ લીધો, અને તે ઉતાવળે પોતાની જગ્યાએ પાછો ગયો.
items.why: そそくさ is leaving or moving quickly, as if to get away from an awkward moment; あたふた (hurried and flustered) is the closest. そわそわ is restless fidgeting while waiting, not moving away. あくせく働く is working hard without rest. はきはき describes clear, lively answers.
items.unit: まとめ 文字・語彙 問題1–4

items.q: 旅行するのも楽しいけれど、家に帰るとほっとする。
items.qr: Ryokou suru no mo tanoshii keredo, ie ni kaeru to hotto suru.
items.en: Travelling is fun too, but when I get home I feel relaxed.
items.hi: घूमना भी मज़ेदार है, पर घर लौटकर सुकून मिलता है।
items.gu: ફરવું પણ મજાનું છે, પણ ઘરે પાછા આવીએ ત્યારે શાંતિ થાય છે.

opts.en: to feel at ease, settle down ✓
to be peaceful (a period, the world)

items.why: ほっとする is a feeling of relief or ease, so 落ち着く (to feel settled, calm) fits. 安定する is about prices, health or a job becoming stable. 無事だ is a fact (nothing bad happened), not a feeling. 平安 describes peaceful times or society, not one person's mood.
items.unit: まとめ 文字・語彙 問題1–4

items.q: 真意
items.qr: shin'i — real intention, true meaning

opts.t: 気まぐれな彼女の真意をくみ取ることは難しい。
opts.r: Kimagure na kanojo no shin'i o kumitoru koto wa muzukashii.
opts.en: It's hard to grasp what my moody girlfriend really means. ✓
opts.hi: मनमौजी उसके असली इरादे को समझना मुश्किल है।
opts.gu: મનમોજી તેના સાચા ઇરાદાને સમજવું અઘરું છે.

opts.t: 親友には、真意を尽くして接している。
opts.r: Shin'yuu ni wa, shin'i o tsukushite sesshite iru.
opts.en: I treat my best friend with all my ~.
opts.hi: मैं अपने पक्के दोस्त से पूरी ~ से पेश आता हूँ।
opts.gu: હું મારા જિગરી મિત્ર સાથે પૂરી ~ થી વર્તું છું.

opts.t: 両親から真意のこもった小包が届き、うれしかった。
opts.r: Ryoushin kara shin'i no komotta kozutsumi ga todoki, ureshikatta.
opts.en: A parcel full of ~ arrived from my parents, and I was happy.
opts.hi: माता-पिता से ~ से भरा पार्सल आया, मुझे ख़ुशी हुई।
opts.gu: માતા-પિતા પાસેથી ~ થી ભરેલું પાર્સલ આવ્યું, મને આનંદ થયો.

opts.t: 興奮していて、つい真意が出てしまった。
opts.r: Koufun shite ite, tsui shin'i ga dete shimatta.
opts.en: I was excited, and my ~ slipped out.
opts.hi: उत्तेजना में मेरा ~ बाहर आ गया।

items.why: 真意 is the true intention behind someone's words or actions, something others try to read: 真意をくみ取る／測りかねる／ただす. 2 needs 誠意 ("sincerity"): 誠意を尽くす. 3 needs 真心 or 心 ("heartfelt care"): 真心のこもった. 4 needs 本音 ("one's real feelings") or 地 ("one's true self"): つい本音が出た.
items.unit: まとめ 文字・語彙 問題1–4

items.q: 懲りる
items.qr: koriru — to learn one's lesson (and not want to do it again)

opts.t: 友人が試験に落ちたと聞いて、受ける前に懲りてしまった。
opts.r: Yuujin ga shiken ni ochita to kiite, ukeru mae ni korite shimatta.
opts.en: Hearing my friend failed the exam, I ~ before even taking it.
opts.hi: दोस्त के फ़ेल होने की बात सुनकर, परीक्षा से पहले ही मैं ~ गया।
opts.gu: મિત્ર નાપાસ થયો એ સાંભળીને, પરીક્ષા પહેલાં જ હું ~ ગયો.

opts.t: 彼は懲りずにまた同じ過ちを繰り返した。
opts.r: Kare wa korizu ni mata onaji ayamachi o kurikaeshita.
opts.en: He didn't learn his lesson and made the same mistake again. ✓
opts.hi: उसने सबक़ नहीं सीखा और वही गलती फिर दोहराई।
opts.gu: તેણે બોધપાઠ ન લીધો અને એ જ ભૂલ ફરી કરી.

opts.t: やりたいようにやったので、何も懲りることはない。
opts.r: Yaritai you ni yatta node, nani mo koriru koto wa nai.
opts.en: I did it the way I wanted, so I have nothing to ~.
opts.hi: मैंने जैसा चाहा वैसा किया, इसलिए ~ की कोई बात नहीं।
opts.gu: મેં જેમ ઇચ્છ્યું તેમ કર્યું, એટલે ~ ની કોઈ વાત નથી.

opts.t: 一度懲りても、二度と繰り返さないようにすればいい。
opts.r: Ichido korite mo, nido to kurikaesanai you ni sureba ii.
opts.en: Even if you ~ once, just make sure not to repeat it.
opts.hi: एक बार ~ भी, बस दोबारा न दोहराना।
opts.gu: એક વાર ~ તોય, બસ ફરી ન કરવું.

items.why: 懲りる needs your own bad experience first, after which you don't want to repeat it; 懲りずに = "without learning". 1 has no own experience — it needs 怖気づく ("lose one's nerve") or やる気をなくす. 3 needs 悔いる／後悔する ("regret"): 何も悔いはない. 4 needs 失敗する ("fail"): 一度失敗しても — it is the mistake you should not repeat, and 懲りる already contains "not repeating".
items.unit: まとめ 文字・語彙 問題1–4

items.q: やけに
items.qr: yake ni — unusually, strangely (so)

opts.t: 争いによってやけに多くの負傷者を出したか忘れてはならない。
opts.r: Arasoi ni yotte yake ni ooku no fushousha o dashita ka wasurete wa naranai.
opts.en: We must not forget ~ many people were injured in the conflict.
opts.hi: हमें नहीं भूलना चाहिए कि संघर्ष में ~ लोग घायल हुए।
opts.gu: આપણે ભૂલવું ન જોઈએ કે સંઘર્ષમાં ~ લોકો ઘાયલ થયા.

opts.t: そんなやけに人を信じては危ないこともある。
opts.r: Sonna yake ni hito o shinjite wa abunai koto mo aru.
opts.en: Trusting people so ~ can be dangerous.
opts.hi: लोगों पर इतना ~ भरोसा करना ख़तरनाक हो सकता है।
opts.gu: લોકો પર આટલો ~ ભરોસો કરવો જોખમી બની શકે.

opts.t: いつも意地悪な彼が、今日はやけに親切で、どうも調子が狂う。
opts.r: Itsumo ijiwaru na kare ga, kyou wa yake ni shinsetsu de, doumo choushi ga kuruu.
opts.en: He's always mean, but today he's strangely kind, and it throws me off. ✓
opts.hi: वह हमेशा बदमिज़ाज रहता है, पर आज अजीब तरह से मेहरबान है, इसलिए मैं उलझन में हूँ।
opts.gu: તે હંમેશાં ખરાબ વર્તે છે, પણ આજે વિચિત્ર રીતે માયાળુ છે, એટલે હું મૂંઝાઉં છું.

opts.t: やけに練習しても、簡単にはうまくはならないものだ。
opts.r: Yake ni renshuu shite mo, kantan ni wa umaku wa naranai mono da.
opts.en: ~ you practise, you don't get good easily.
opts.hi: चाहे ~ अभ्यास करो, आसानी से माहिर नहीं होते।
opts.gu: ગમે તેટલો ~ અભ્યાસ કરો, સહેલાઈથી પારંગત ન થવાય.

items.why: やけに is a casual adverb for something that is "unusually ~, in a way that feels odd" right now: 今日はやけに静かだ／やけに親切だ. 1 needs いかに ("how many"): いかに多くの…か. 2 needs むやみに or やたらに ("indiscriminately"); そんな also clashes. 4 needs いくら ("no matter how much"): いくら練習しても.
items.unit: まとめ 文字・語彙 問題1–4

items.q: 犯人は客の一人を人質に取って立てこもっている。
items.qr: Hannin wa kyaku no hitori o hitojichi ni totte tatekomotte iru.
items.en: The criminal has taken one of the customers hostage and has barricaded himself inside.
items.hi: अपराधी ने ग्राहकों में से एक को बंधक बना लिया है और अंदर मोर्चा बाँधकर बैठा है।
items.gu: ગુનેગારે ગ્રાહકોમાંથી એકને બંધક બનાવી લીધો છે અને અંદર ભરાઈને બેઠો છે.
items.why: 人質 uses the native (訓) reading ひと for 人. 質 is read しち (as in 質屋 shichiya, "pawnshop"), and here it becomes voiced: じち. The other options mix in the on-reading じん, or keep 質 as the common しつ (質問). They look possible, but they are not real words. Set phrase: 人質に取る "take as a hostage".

items.q: 知人が仲介してくれたおかげで、問題が早く解決した。
items.qr: Chijin ga chuukai shite kureta okage de, mondai ga hayaku kaiketsu shita.
items.en: Thanks to an acquaintance acting as a go-between, the problem was solved quickly.
items.hi: एक परिचित ने मध्यस्थता की, इसकी वजह से समस्या जल्दी सुलझ गई।
items.gu: એક ઓળખીતાએ મધ્યસ્થી કરી, તેના કારણે સમસ્યા જલદી ઉકલી ગઈ.

opts.en: brokerage (a different word, written 仲買)
not a real reading of 仲介
opts.hi: 仲介 का सही उच्चारण नहीं
opts.gu: 仲介 નું સાચું ઉચ્ચારણ નથી

items.why: Both kanji use on-readings: 仲 = ちゅう (仲裁 chuusai) and 介 = かい (紹介, 介護). The かい stays unvoiced, so the answer is ちゅうかい, not ちゅうがい. The trap is option 1, なかがい. It is a real word, but it is 仲買 (a broker), with 買 "buy", not 介.

items.q: 各ページの右下にイラストを挿入することにした。
items.qr: Kaku peeji no migishita ni irasuto o sounyuu suru koto ni shita.
items.en: We decided to insert an illustration at the bottom right of each page.
items.hi: हमने हर पेज के नीचे दाईं ओर एक चित्र डालने का फ़ैसला किया।
items.gu: અમે દરેક પાનાની નીચે જમણી બાજુ એક ચિત્ર મૂકવાનું નક્કી કર્યું.

opts.en: moving in, transfer (a different word, 転入)
injection, pouring in (a different word, 注入)
throwing in, investing (a different word, 投入)

items.why: 挿 is read そう (on) or さ-す (kun): 挿す "to insert", 挿絵 "illustration". All four options are 〜にゅう words that end in 入. The other three are real words, but each one uses a different first kanji (転・注・投). For this question type, picture the kanji of each option. Do not choose just because a reading "sounds familiar".

items.q: 最近、運動不足のため体力が衰えてきたようだ。
items.qr: Saikin, undou busoku no tame tairyoku ga otoroete kita you da.
items.en: Lately my physical strength seems to have been declining because I don't get enough exercise.
items.hi: लगता है कि आजकल व्यायाम की कमी से मेरी शारीरिक ताक़त घटने लगी है।
items.gu: લાગે છે કે હમણાં કસરતના અભાવે મારી શારીરિક શક્તિ ઘટવા લાગી છે.
items.why: 衰 = おとろ-える, or すい in 衰退 (decline) and 老衰 (old age). 萎える also means "to weaken", so the meaning alone could mislead you. But it is a different kanji. 鍛える is the opposite idea (体力を鍛える "build up strength"). Look-alike warning: 衰 vs 哀 (あわ-れ, "pity") vs 喪 (も, "mourning").

items.q: 同級生の姿を見つけたが、人込みに紛れて見失ってしまった。
items.qr: Doukyuusei no sugata o mitsuketa ga, hitogomi ni magirete miushinatte shimatta.
items.en: I spotted a classmate, but he disappeared into the crowd and I lost sight of him.
items.hi: मैंने अपने सहपाठी को देखा, लेकिन वह भीड़ में घुल-मिल गया और मेरी नज़रों से ओझल हो गया।
items.gu: મેં મારા સહપાઠીને જોયો, પણ તે ભીડમાં ભળી ગયો અને મારી નજરથી ઓઝલ થઈ ગયો.
items.why: 紛 = まぎ-れる, or ふん in 紛失 (loss) and 紛争 (dispute). 人込みに紛れる "vanish into a crowd" is a set phrase. The trap is もまれて: 人込みにもまれる ("get jostled in a crowd") is also natural Japanese, but it is written 揉まれる. The kanji tells you the answer, not the collocation.

items.q: 暑い中の作業が続き、首筋から汗が滴る。
items.qr: Atsui naka no sagyou ga tsuzuki, kubisuji kara ase ga shitataru.
items.en: The work in the heat goes on and on, and sweat drips from the back of my neck.
items.hi: गर्मी में काम लगातार चलता रहा, और गर्दन के पीछे से पसीना टपक रहा है।
items.gu: ગરમીમાં કામ સતત ચાલતું રહ્યું, અને ગરદનની પાછળથી પરસેવો ટપકે છે.
items.why: 滴 = したた-る, しずく ("a drop"), and てき in 水滴 and 点滴 (IV drip). 汗が垂れる also means "sweat drips", so the meaning fits. But this question tests the reading of 滴る, and 垂れる uses the kanji 垂. たぎる and あふれる do not suit 汗 coming from 首筋.

items.q: この罪は、一生かけても償えるものではない。
items.qr: Kono tsumi wa, isshou kakete mo tsugunaeru mono de wa nai.
items.en: This crime is not something you can atone for, even if you spent your whole life trying.
items.hi: यह अपराध ऐसा नहीं है जिसका प्रायश्चित पूरी ज़िंदगी लगाकर भी किया जा सके।
items.gu: આ ગુનો એવો નથી કે જેનું પ્રાયશ્ચિત આખી જિંદગી લગાવીને પણ થઈ શકે.
items.why: 償 = つぐな-う, or しょう in 補償 and 賠償 (compensation). 罪を償う "atone for a crime" is a fixed collocation. まかなう (賄う) has a similar 〜なう shape and is a common N1 word, but it means paying for something: 費用を賄う "cover the costs". Note that 償 has the 賞 part on the right, so the on-reading しょう is easy to guess.

items.q: 我々の提案はあえなく先方に拒まれてしまった。
items.qr: Wareware no teian wa aenaku senpou ni kobamarete shimatta.
items.en: Our proposal was flatly turned down by the other side.
items.hi: हमारे प्रस्ताव को सामने वाले पक्ष ने आसानी से ठुकरा दिया।
items.gu: અમારા પ્રસ્તાવને સામેના પક્ષે સહેલાઈથી ફગાવી દીધો.

opts.hi: ईर्ष्या का शिकार होकर (妬まれて)
अफ़सोस के साथ याद किए जाकर (惜しまれて)
opts.gu: અફસોસ સાથે યાદ કરાઈને (惜しまれて)

items.why: 拒 = こば-む, or きょ in 拒否 and 拒絶. The main trap is はばむ (阻む, 阻止 "prevention"). It is a 3-mora 〜ばむ verb with a similar meaning, "to block". Remember: 拒む = say no to a request or proposal, 阻む = physically or practically block progress (行く手を阻む). The adverb あえなく means "all too easily, sadly".

items.q: パーティーは和やかな雰囲気に包まれていた。
items.qr: Paatii wa nagoyaka na fun'iki ni tsutsumarete ita.
items.en: The party had a warm, friendly atmosphere throughout.
items.hi: पार्टी में एक सौहार्दपूर्ण, आरामदायक माहौल छाया हुआ था।
items.gu: પાર્ટીમાં સૌહાર્દપૂર્ણ, હળવું વાતાવરણ છવાયેલું હતું.
items.why: 和 has many readings: わ (平和), なご-む, なご-やか, やわ-らぐ. All four options are 〜やか adjectives, so match the kanji: 和やか, 艶やか, 淑やか, 健やか. Collocations: 和やかな雰囲気／ムード, 艶やかな着物, しとやかな女性, 健やかな成長.

items.q: さまざまな指標によって、今後の経済の（ ）を探ろうとしている。
items.qr: Samazama na shihyou ni yotte, kongo no keizai no (___) o saguroo to shite iru.
items.en: They are using various indicators to find out which way the economy will move next.
items.hi: तरह-तरह के सूचकांकों के ज़रिए वे यह पता लगाने की कोशिश कर रहे हैं कि आगे अर्थव्यवस्था किस दिशा में जाएगी।
items.gu: વિવિધ સૂચકાંકો દ્વારા તેઓ એ જાણવાનો પ્રયાસ કરી રહ્યા છે કે આગળ અર્થતંત્ર કઈ દિશામાં જશે.
items.why: 動向 means the way something that keeps changing is moving. It goes naturally with 探る, 見守る and 注視する, and with subjects like 経済, 市場 and 世論. 傾向 is a pattern you have already observed (〜する傾向がある). Here we are looking forward (今後) with indicators. 意向 is a person's wish (社長の意向), which an economy cannot have. 指向 means "orientation" (上昇志向 is written with 志, and 指向性 means directionality).

items.q: 合意にあたっては、互いの主張の（ ）を埋める必要がある。
items.qr: Goui ni atatte wa, tagai no shuchou no (___) o umeru hitsuyou ga aru.
items.en: To reach an agreement, we need to bridge the gap between our two positions.
items.hi: सहमति तक पहुँचने के लिए दोनों पक्षों के दावों के बीच की खाई पाटनी ज़रूरी है।
items.gu: સમજૂતી સુધી પહોંચવા બંને પક્ષોના દાવાઓ વચ્ચેની ખાઈ પૂરવી જરૂરી છે.
items.why: 溝 literally means a ditch. Figuratively it is the gap in feelings or opinions between two sides, and its fixed partners are 溝を埋める (bridge the gap) and 溝が深まる (the gap widens). 間 is too neutral to be "filled" in this sense. 幅 collocates with 広げる/狭める. 境 is a line, not a gap.

items.q: 悪天候により、飛行機の到着が（ ）遅れている。
items.qr: Akutenkou ni yori, hikouki no touchaku ga (___) okurete iru.
items.en: Because of the bad weather, flight arrivals are delayed across the board.
items.hi: ख़राब मौसम के कारण लगभग सभी उड़ानें देर से पहुँच रही हैं।
items.gu: ખરાબ હવામાનને કારણે લગભગ બધી ફ્લાઇટ્સ મોડી પહોંચી રહી છે.

opts.hi: लगभग सभी, एक के बाद एक

items.why: The blank comes right before a verb (遅れている), so it needs an adverb. 軒並み is the only one used on its own as an adverb ("all of them, one after another"). The other 〜並み words are nouns or な-adjectives with fixed partners: 足並みをそろえる (act in step), 人並みの生活 (an ordinary life), 月並みな表現 (a clichéd phrase).

items.q: 長時間にわたる作業がようやく終わり、上司に（ ）の言葉をかけられた。
items.qr: Choujikan ni wataru sagyou ga youyaku owari, joushi ni (___) no kotoba o kakerareta.
items.en: The long job was finally finished, and my boss thanked me for all my hard work.
items.hi: लंबे समय तक चला काम आख़िरकार ख़त्म हुआ, और बॉस ने मेरी मेहनत की सराहना के शब्द कहे।
items.gu: લાંબા સમય સુધી ચાલેલું કામ આખરે પૂરું થયું, અને બોસે મારી મહેનતની કદરના શબ્દો કહ્યા.
items.why: The work is already finished (ようやく終わり). ねぎらう is how you thank someone, usually someone of lower status, for effort they have completed: お疲れさま, よく頑張ったね. 励まし is given before or during a struggle. 慰め is given after something sad or after a failure. 手当て does not combine with 〜の言葉.

items.q: 他人と競わず、（ ）で人生を歩んでいきたいと思います。
items.qr: Tanin to kisowazu, (___) de jinsei o ayunde ikitai to omoimasu.
items.en: I want to go through life at my own pace, without competing with other people.
items.hi: मैं दूसरों से होड़ किए बिना, अपनी रफ़्तार से ज़िंदगी जीना चाहता हूँ।
items.gu: હું બીજાઓ સાથે હરીફાઈ કર્યા વિના, મારી પોતાની ગતિએ જીવન જીવવા માંગું છું.
items.why: 他人と競わず ("without competing with others") points directly to マイペース, which means doing things at your own speed without caring about others. マイペースで〜する is the set pattern. リラックスして would need して, not で. プライベートで means "privately, off duty", which is a different idea.

items.q: 進学について両親に反対されたが、自分の意思を（ ）。
items.qr: Shingaku ni tsuite ryoushin ni hantai sareta ga, jibun no ishi o (___).
items.en: My parents were against me going on to further study, but I stuck to my decision.
items.hi: आगे की पढ़ाई को लेकर माता-पिता ने विरोध किया, फिर भी मैं अपने इरादे पर डटा रहा।
items.gu: આગળ ભણવા બાબતે માતા-પિતાએ વિરોધ કર્યો, છતાં હું મારા નિર્ણય પર અડગ રહ્યો.

opts.hi: (किसी भूमिका में) पूरी तरह लगा रहा

opts.en: did nothing but ~ from start to finish
opts.hi: शुरू से अंत तक (सिर्फ़ वही) करता रहा
opts.gu: શરૂથી અંત સુધી (ફક્ત એ જ) કરતો રહ્યો

items.why: 意思／信念／主張を貫く ("hold to your will to the end") takes the particle を, exactly as in the sentence. 徹する and 終始する take に: 裏方に徹する (stay fully in a support role), 言い訳に終始する (do nothing but make excuses). 刺し通す is only physical (needle, sword). Checking the particle is a quick way to eliminate options.

items.q: 競合相手とはいえ、さまざまな策を（ ）ことは必ずしもいいことではない。
items.qr: Kyougou aite to wa ie, samazama na saku o (___) koto wa kanarazushimo ii koto de wa nai.
items.en: They may be a competitor, but plotting all kinds of schemes against them is not always a good thing.
items.hi: भले ही वह प्रतिस्पर्धी हो, उसके ख़िलाफ़ तरह-तरह की चालें चलना हमेशा अच्छी बात नहीं है।
items.gu: ભલે તે હરીફ હોય, તેની સામે જાતજાતની યુક્તિઓ ઘડવી હંમેશાં સારી વાત નથી.
items.why: 策を巡らす ("think up schemes, plot") is an idiom, like 思いを巡らす ("let your thoughts wander over"). The other three are about physically surrounding or turning something. 取り巻く and 囲む take people or places as the object (彼を取り巻く環境). 回す appears in 手を回す ("pull strings"), but 策を回す is not used.

items.q: 各部署との調整が必要で、まだ（ ）計画しか立っていない。
items.qr: Kaku busho to no chousei ga hitsuyou de, mada (___) keikaku shika tatte inai.
items.en: We still have to coordinate with each department, so for now there is only a rough plan.
items.hi: हर विभाग से तालमेल बिठाना अभी बाक़ी है, इसलिए फ़िलहाल सिर्फ़ एक मोटी-मोटी योजना ही बनी है।
items.gu: દરેક વિભાગ સાથે સંકલન હજુ બાકી છે, તેથી હાલ માત્ર એક અંદાજિત યોજના જ બની છે.

opts.hi: बड़े कद-काठी का; बड़े डिज़ाइन वाला

items.why: The details still depend on talks with each department (まだ〜しか), so the plan exists only in outline: 大まかな計画. 大幅な describes the size of a change or cut (大幅な変更／値下げ), not a plan's detail. 大柄な describes a body or a pattern on cloth. 大半の計画 would mean "most of the plans", which does not fit しか.

items.q: 知っている人ならまだしも、初対面の相手に対し、（ ）態度をとるとは信じられない。
items.qr: Shitte iru hito nara madashimo, shotaimen no aite ni taishi, (___) taido o toru to wa shinjirarenai.
items.en: With someone you know it might be OK, but I can't believe he acted so overly familiar with a person he had only just met.
items.hi: जान-पहचान वाले के साथ तो फिर भी ठीक, पर पहली बार मिले व्यक्ति के साथ इतनी बेतकल्लुफ़ी दिखाना — यक़ीन नहीं होता।
items.gu: ઓળખીતા સાથે તો હજી ઠીક, પણ પહેલી વાર મળેલી વ્યક્તિ સાથે આટલું વધારે પડતું ઘનિષ્ઠ વર્તન — માનવામાં નથી આવતું.
items.why: 〜ならまだしも means "X would be one thing, but…". So the attitude is acceptable with people you know but not with someone you have just met (初対面). That describes being too familiar, too soon: なれなれしい (from 慣れる). The other three repeated-syllable adjectives describe noise, youth or absurdity, and none of these depend on how well you know the person.

items.q: 彼は作家としてはまだまだ（ ）表現が多いが、人の心を打つストーリーが書ける。
items.qr: Kare wa sakka to shite wa madamada (___) hyougen ga ooi ga, hito no kokoro o utsu sutoorii ga kakeru.
items.en: As a writer, his wording is still often clumsy, but he can write stories that touch people's hearts.
items.hi: लेखक के तौर पर उसकी भाषा में अभी भी काफ़ी कच्चापन है, पर वह दिल को छू लेने वाली कहानियाँ लिख सकता है।
items.gu: લેખક તરીકે તેની ભાષામાં હજુ ઘણી કચાશ છે, પણ તે દિલને સ્પર્શી જાય એવી વાર્તાઓ લખી શકે છે.
items.why: つたない (拙い) describes poor-quality skill or output: 拙い文章／表現／日本語. It fits "still clumsy as a writer (まだまだ)". ふつつか is used almost only in humble set phrases about yourself or your family (ふつつか者ですが). 不得意 describes a person's weak subject (作文が不得意だ), not an expression. つれない describes a cold attitude toward someone.

items.q: そんなに焦っていては、うまくいくものもいかなくなってしまう。
items.qr: Sonna ni asette ite wa, umaku iku mono mo ikanaku natte shimau.
items.en: If you are in such a rush, even things that would go well will go wrong.
items.hi: अगर तुम इतनी हड़बड़ी में रहोगे, तो जो काम ठीक हो सकता था, वह भी बिगड़ जाएगा।
items.gu: જો તું આટલી ઉતાવળમાં રહીશ, તો જે કામ સારું થઈ શકે તે પણ બગડી જશે.
items.why: 焦る means you are impatient and rush because time is short or things are not going well. 慌てる is the closest: acting in a hurry and losing your calm. 悩む and 苦しむ are about inner worry or pain, not speed. 怒る is anger. The second half (うまくいくものもいかなくなる) is the classic result of rushing.

items.q: 買うつもりはなかったが、子どもにせがまれて、つい買ってしまった。
items.qr: Kau tsumori wa nakatta ga, kodomo ni segamarete, tsui katte shimatta.
items.en: I had no plan to buy it, but my child kept begging, and I ended up buying it.
items.hi: ख़रीदने का इरादा नहीं था, पर बच्चे ने ज़िद करके माँगा, तो आख़िर ख़रीद ही लिया।
items.gu: ખરીદવાનો ઇરાદો નહોતો, પણ બાળકે જીદ કરીને માગ્યું, એટલે આખરે ખરીદી જ લીધું.
items.why: せがむ and ねだる both mean asking again and again for something you want, typically a child to a parent. Both are used here in the passive (〜られて): "being begged by the child". せかす (急かす) also sounds similar and also pressures someone, but it means "make someone hurry", not "ask for a thing". もてなす (welcome a guest) and 嘆く (grieve) do not fit.

items.q: 新しい駅ビルは、2年後に完成の見込みだ。
items.qr: Atarashii eki biru wa, ni-nen go ni kansei no mikomi da.
items.en: The new station building is expected to be completed in two years.
items.hi: नई स्टेशन बिल्डिंग के दो साल बाद पूरी होने की संभावना है।
items.gu: નવી સ્ટેશન બિલ્ડિંગ બે વર્ષ પછી પૂરી થવાની શક્યતા છે.
items.why: 〜の見込みだ and 〜の見通しだ both mean "it is expected that ~", as in news reports about schedules. All four options start with 見, so you must know each one. 見積もり is a money estimate (見積書 "quotation"). 見極め is judging something carefully. 見晴らし is a scenic view (見晴らしがいい).

items.q: 定年後は田舎に戻って、のどかな生活を送りたいと思っていた。
items.qr: Teinen go wa inaka ni modotte, nodoka na seikatsu o okuritai to omotte ita.
items.en: I was thinking that after retirement I would go back to the countryside and live a calm, peaceful life.
items.hi: मैं सोच रहा था कि रिटायरमेंट के बाद गाँव लौटकर शांत, सुकून-भरी ज़िंदगी बिताऊँगा।
items.gu: હું વિચારતો હતો કે નિવૃત્તિ પછી ગામડે પાછો જઈને શાંત, નિરાંતવાળું જીવન જીવીશ.
items.why: のどか describes a slow, quiet, peaceful scene or life with no stress, often in the countryside. 穏やか ("calm, without trouble") is the nearest. A country life may also be 健康的 or 自由, but those are different ideas, not paraphrases. さわやか is about a fresh feeling (weather, a smile).

items.q: フロントで働く人は、さまざまな問題にすぐ対応できる人物が好ましいと思う。
items.qr: Furonto de hataraku hito wa, samazama na mondai ni sugu taiou dekiru jinbutsu ga konomashii to omou.
items.en: For people working at the front desk, I think someone who can deal with all kinds of problems at once is desirable.
items.hi: मुझे लगता है कि फ़्रंट डेस्क पर काम करने के लिए ऐसा व्यक्ति बेहतर है जो तरह-तरह की समस्याएँ तुरंत सँभाल सके।
items.gu: મને લાગે છે કે ફ્રન્ટ ડેસ્ક પર કામ કરવા માટે એવી વ્યક્તિ ઇચ્છનીય છે જે જાતજાતની સમસ્યાઓ તરત સંભાળી શકે.
items.why: Here 好ましい does not mean "likeable". It means "the kind that should be chosen", which is exactly 望ましい. The sentence is a condition for a job, not praise of a real person, so 素晴らしい does not paraphrase it. 喜ばしい is for happy events (喜ばしい知らせ). 目覚ましい is for fast progress (目覚ましい発展).

items.q: 式典会場の周りは、物々しい警戒態勢が敷かれている。
items.qr: Shikiten kaijou no mawari wa, monomonoshii keikai taisei ga shikarete iru.
items.en: Very tight security has been set up around the ceremony venue.
items.hi: समारोह स्थल के चारों ओर कड़ी सुरक्षा व्यवस्था लगाई गई है।
items.gu: સમારોહ સ્થળની આસપાસ કડક સુરક્ષા વ્યવસ્થા ગોઠવવામાં આવી છે.
items.why: 物々しい describes security or equipment that looks heavy and serious, almost too much. With 警戒／警備, the paraphrase is 厳重な ("strict, tight"). The trap is 物騒な: it shares the 物 kanji and is about danger, but it means the place is unsafe, not that the guarding is strong. 勇ましい and ずうずうしい describe people.

items.q: 休みの日は、もっぱら子どもの相手をして過ごしています。
items.qr: Yasumi no hi wa, moppara kodomo no aite o shite sugoshite imasu.
items.en: On my days off, I mostly spend the time looking after and playing with my children.
items.hi: छुट्टी के दिन मैं ज़्यादातर बच्चों के साथ समय बिताता हूँ।
items.gu: રજાના દિવસે હું મોટે ભાગે બાળકો સાથે સમય વિતાવું છું.
items.why: もっぱら (専ら) means "almost entirely, mostly (doing one thing)". 主に is the closest. ひたむきに is a trap: it is also about focusing on one thing, but it describes the attitude (earnest effort), not how most of the time is used. しきりに is "again and again" and 盛んに is "vigorously, popularly".

items.q: そんな不公平な要求に対しては、断固反対するべきだ。
items.qr: Sonna fukouhei na youkyuu ni taishite wa, danko hantai suru beki da.
items.en: We should firmly oppose such an unfair demand.
items.hi: ऐसी अन्यायपूर्ण माँग का हमें दृढ़ता से विरोध करना चाहिए।
items.gu: આવી અન્યાયી માગણીનો આપણે દૃઢતાથી વિરોધ કરવો જોઈએ.
items.why: 断固 (断固として) means doing something with a firm, unshakable will. きっぱり ("clearly, without hesitation") is the match, as in きっぱり断る／反対する. The four options all have the 〜っ〜り shape, so meaning decides: さっぱり is "fresh" or, with a negative, "not at all"; すっかり is "completely"; ぎっしり is "packed full".

items.q: 経済的な発展に伴い、国民の生活も徐々に豊かになった。
items.qr: Keizaiteki na hatten ni tomonai, kokumin no seikatsu mo jojo ni yutaka ni natta.
items.en: Along with economic development, people's lives also gradually became better off.
items.hi: आर्थिक विकास के साथ-साथ लोगों का जीवन भी धीरे-धीरे समृद्ध हुआ।
items.gu: આર્થિક વિકાસની સાથે લોકોનું જીવન પણ ધીમે ધીમે સમૃદ્ધ થયું.
items.why: 徐々に means "slowly, step by step", the same as だんだん. どんどん also describes a change that continues, but it is fast and strong, the opposite feeling. かなり and 少し describe the amount of change, not its speed.

items.q: ビジョン
items.qr: bijon — vision (a plan or picture of the future)

opts.t: 高台からのビジョンは遠くまで見えてとてもいい。
opts.r: Takadai kara no bijon wa tooku made miete totemo ii.
opts.en: The ~ from the hill is great because you can see far.
opts.hi: पहाड़ी से ~ बहुत अच्छा है, दूर तक दिखता है।
opts.gu: ટેકરી પરથી ~ સરસ છે, દૂર સુધી દેખાય છે.

opts.t: 技術の進歩によって、テレビのビジョンはよくなっている。
opts.r: Gijutsu no shinpo ni yotte, terebi no bijon wa yoku natte iru.
opts.en: Thanks to better technology, TV ~ is improving.
opts.hi: तकनीक की प्रगति से टीवी का ~ बेहतर हो रहा है।
opts.gu: ટેક્નોલોજીની પ્રગતિથી ટીવીનું ~ સુધરી રહ્યું છે.

opts.t: 夜間の運転はビジョンが狭くなりがちなので気をつけたほうがいい。
opts.r: Yakan no unten wa bijon ga semaku narigachi na node ki o tsuketa hou ga ii.
opts.en: When driving at night your ~ tends to get narrow, so be careful.
opts.hi: रात में गाड़ी चलाते समय ~ संकरा हो जाता है, सावधान रहें।
opts.gu: રાત્રે ગાડી ચલાવતાં ~ સાંકડું થઈ જાય છે, સાવચેત રહો.

opts.t: 代表にはこれからのビジョンを明確に示してもらいたい。
opts.r: Daihyou ni wa korekara no bijon o meikaku ni shimeshite moraitai.
opts.en: I want the leader to show a clear vision for the future. ✓
opts.hi: मैं चाहता हूँ कि प्रतिनिधि आगे की दृष्टि (योजना) साफ़-साफ़ बताएँ।
opts.gu: હું ઇચ્છું છું કે પ્રતિનિધિ આગળની દૃષ્ટિ (યોજના) સ્પષ્ટ રીતે રજૂ કરે.

items.why: In Japanese, ビジョン is almost always a picture of the future: a plan, goal or direction (将来のビジョン, 経営ビジョン). It is not used for things you see with your eyes. 1 needs 眺め or 景色 ("view"). 2 needs 画質 or 映像 ("picture quality"). 3 needs 視野 ("field of vision"): 視野が狭くなる.

items.q: 余地
items.qr: yochi — room, scope (for doing something)

opts.t: 今の生活に経済的な余地はない。
opts.r: Ima no seikatsu ni keizaiteki na yochi wa nai.
opts.en: There is no financial ~ in my life now.
opts.hi: अभी की ज़िंदगी में आर्थिक ~ नहीं है।

opts.t: この件に関しては、何を言われても弁解の余地はない。
opts.r: Kono ken ni kanshite wa, nani o iwarete mo benkai no yochi wa nai.
opts.en: On this matter, whatever they say to me, there is no room for excuses. ✓
opts.hi: इस मामले में, कोई कुछ भी कहे, सफ़ाई देने की कोई गुंजाइश नहीं है।
opts.gu: આ બાબતમાં, કોઈ ગમે તે કહે, બચાવ કરવાનો કોઈ અવકાશ નથી.

opts.t: 人気の舞台だが、当日でも若干の余地があるそうだ。
opts.r: Ninki no butai da ga, toujitsu demo jakkan no yochi ga aru sou da.
opts.en: It's a popular show, but I hear there is a little ~ even on the day.
opts.hi: नाटक लोकप्रिय है, पर सुना है उसी दिन भी थोड़ी ~ होती है।
opts.gu: નાટક લોકપ્રિય છે, પણ સાંભળ્યું છે કે તે જ દિવસે પણ થોડી ~ હોય છે.

opts.t: まだ走れるが、明日のために余地を残しておくことにする。
opts.r: Mada hashireru ga, ashita no tame ni yochi o nokoshite oku koto ni suru.
opts.en: I can still run, but I'll keep some ~ for tomorrow.
opts.hi: मैं अभी दौड़ सकता हूँ, पर कल के लिए थोड़ी ~ बचाकर रखूँगा।
opts.gu: હું હજી દોડી શકું છું, પણ કાલ માટે થોડી ~ બચાવી રાખીશ.

items.why: 余地 is "room for an action or a possibility", and it usually comes after 〜の: 弁解の余地はない ("no excuse is possible"), 疑問の余地がない, 改善の余地がある. 1 needs 余裕 ("financial leeway"): 経済的な余裕. 3 needs 空席 or 残席 ("free seats"). 4 needs 余力 or 体力 ("energy in reserve"): 余力を残す. The trap is 余裕, which is the most common confusion with 余地.

items.q: 脅かす
items.qr: obiyakasu — to threaten, endanger

opts.t: 弟は姉を脅かそうとドアの陰に隠れて待っていた。
opts.r: Otouto wa ane o obiyakasou to doa no kage ni kakurete matte ita.
opts.en: The younger brother hid behind the door, waiting to ~ his sister.
opts.hi: छोटा भाई बहन को ~ के लिए दरवाज़े के पीछे छिपकर बैठा था।
opts.gu: નાનો ભાઈ બહેનને ~ માટે બારણા પાછળ છુપાઈને બેઠો હતો.

opts.t: 隣国との対立は我々の安全を脅かすものだ。
opts.r: Ringoku to no tairitsu wa wareware no anzen o obiyakasu mono da.
opts.en: The conflict with the neighbouring country threatens our safety. ✓
opts.hi: पड़ोसी देश से टकराव हमारी सुरक्षा को ख़तरे में डालता है।
opts.gu: પડોશી દેશ સાથેનો સંઘર્ષ આપણી સલામતીને જોખમમાં મૂકે છે.

opts.t: 人目を脅かすような行動は慎んでください。
opts.r: Hitome o obiyakasu you na koudou wa tsutsushinde kudasai.
opts.en: Please avoid behaviour that ~ people's eyes.
opts.hi: ऐसा व्यवहार न करें जो लोगों की नज़रों को ~।
opts.gu: એવું વર્તન ન કરો જે લોકોની નજરને ~.

opts.t: 部長面接はかなり厳しいと先輩に脅かされた。
opts.r: Buchou mensetsu wa kanari kibishii to senpai ni obiyakasareta.
opts.en: My senior ~ me that the interview with the department head is very tough.
opts.hi: सीनियर ने मुझे ~ कि विभाग प्रमुख का इंटरव्यू बहुत कड़ा होता है।
opts.gu: સિનિયરે મને ~ કે વિભાગ વડાનો ઇન્ટરવ્યૂ બહુ કડક હોય છે.

items.why: Read おびやかす, 脅かす means putting a position, safety or life in danger: 安全／生活／地位を脅かす. The same kanji read おどかす means "to scare someone" or "to warn by frightening". That is the meaning in 1 (jump out and scare) and 4 (scare with a warning), so those need おどかす, not おびやかす. 3 needs 引く or 驚かす: 人目を引く行動 ("behaviour that attracts attention").

items.q: 見据える
items.qr: misueru — to fix one's eyes on; to keep (the future) firmly in view

opts.t: 幼い子どもが転んで怪我をしないように、母は温かくじっと見据えた。
opts.r: Osanai kodomo ga koronde kega o shinai you ni, haha wa atataku jitto misueta.
opts.en: So that her little child would not fall and get hurt, the mother ~ warmly and steadily.
opts.hi: छोटा बच्चा गिरकर चोट न खाए, इसलिए माँ ने प्यार से एकटक ~।
opts.gu: નાનું બાળક પડીને વાગે નહીં, એટલે માએ પ્રેમથી એકીટશે ~.

opts.t: 来場者は人気スターの登場を喜び、穴が開くほど見据えていた。
opts.r: Raijousha wa ninki sutaa no toujou o yorokobi, ana ga aku hodo misuete ita.
opts.en: The visitors were delighted at the star's entrance and ~ (her) hard enough to burn a hole.
opts.hi: दर्शक लोकप्रिय स्टार के आने से ख़ुश हुए और एकटक ~ रहे।
opts.gu: પ્રેક્ષકો લોકપ્રિય સ્ટારના આગમનથી ખુશ થયા અને એકીટશે ~ રહ્યા.

opts.t: 懐かしい映画がテレビで放送されていたので見据えていた。
opts.r: Natsukashii eiga ga terebi de housou sarete ita node misuete ita.
opts.en: An old film I loved was on TV, so I was ~ it.
opts.hi: एक पुरानी पसंदीदा फ़िल्म टीवी पर आ रही थी, इसलिए मैं उसे ~ रहा था।
opts.gu: એક જૂની ગમતી ફિલ્મ ટીવી પર આવતી હતી, એટલે હું તેને ~ રહ્યો હતો.

opts.t: 将来を見据えた後継者選びが行われた。
opts.r: Shourai o misueta koukeisha erabi ga okonawareta.
opts.en: A successor was chosen with the future firmly in view. ✓
opts.hi: भविष्य को ध्यान में रखकर उत्तराधिकारी का चुनाव किया गया।
opts.gu: ભવિષ્યને ધ્યાનમાં રાખીને અનુગામીની પસંદગી કરવામાં આવી.

items.why: 見据える is used mostly with abstract objects: 将来／現実／目標を見据える, "decide while looking clearly at the future or the facts". When it is literal, it is a hard, serious stare, not a warm or happy look. 1 needs 見守った ("watched over"). 2 needs 見つめていた ("gazed at"; 穴が開くほど見つめる is the idiom). 3 needs 見入っていた ("was absorbed in watching").

items.q: 素朴
items.qr: soboku — simple, plain, unpretentious

opts.t: 提出された論文には素朴な間違いが多く、見直しが必要だ。
opts.r: Teishutsu sareta ronbun ni wa soboku na machigai ga ooku, minaoshi ga hitsuyou da.
opts.en: The submitted paper has many ~ mistakes and needs checking again.
opts.hi: जमा किए गए शोधपत्र में कई ~ ग़लतियाँ हैं, दोबारा जाँचना ज़रूरी है।
opts.gu: જમા કરેલા સંશોધનપત્રમાં ઘણી ~ ભૂલો છે, ફરી તપાસવું જરૂરી છે.

opts.t: 最近の子どもは昔ながらの素朴な遊びには関心がないようだ。
opts.r: Saikin no kodomo wa mukashinagara no soboku na asobi ni wa kanshin ga nai you da.
opts.en: Children today don't seem interested in simple, old-fashioned games. ✓
opts.hi: आजकल के बच्चों को पुराने ज़माने के सीधे-सादे खेलों में रुचि नहीं लगती।
opts.gu: આજકાલનાં બાળકોને જૂના જમાનાની સાદી રમતોમાં રસ નથી લાગતો.

opts.t: 抗議に対する事務所の対応は、素朴で時間のかかるものだった。
opts.r: Kougi ni taisuru jimusho no taiou wa, soboku de jikan no kakaru mono datta.
opts.en: The office's response to the complaint was ~ and slow.
opts.hi: शिकायत पर दफ़्तर का जवाब ~ और धीमा था।
opts.gu: ફરિયાદ પર ઑફિસનો જવાબ ~ અને ધીમો હતો.

opts.t: 上司の意見には素朴に従う。
opts.r: Joushi no iken ni wa soboku ni shitagau.
opts.hi: मैं बॉस की राय को ~ मान लेता हूँ।
opts.gu: હું બોસનો અભિપ્રાય ~ માની લઉં છું.

items.why: 素朴 is a good, warm word: simple and natural, without decoration (素朴な味／人柄／遊び／疑問). 1 needs 初歩的な ("basic, elementary") or 単純な: 初歩的な間違い. 3 needs 事務的 or 形式的 (or 杜撰) for a cold, slow official reply. 4 needs 素直に ("obediently, without arguing"). 素直 vs 素朴 is the classic pair: both have 素, but 素直 is about attitude, 素朴 about simplicity.

items.q: 潔い
items.qr: isagiyoi — manly, graceful; accepting (blame, defeat) without excuses

opts.t: 毎朝、欠かさず掃除をしているので部屋の中が潔い。
opts.r: Maiasa, kakasazu souji o shite iru node heya no naka ga isagiyoi.
opts.en: I clean every morning without fail, so the room is ~.
opts.hi: मैं हर सुबह बिना चूके सफ़ाई करता हूँ, इसलिए कमरा ~ है।
opts.gu: હું દરરોજ સવારે ચૂક્યા વગર સફાઈ કરું છું, એટલે રૂમ ~ છે.

opts.t: 今日は天気がよく、潔い風が吹いている。
opts.r: Kyou wa tenki ga yoku, isagiyoi kaze ga fuite iru.
opts.en: The weather is nice today and a ~ breeze is blowing.
opts.hi: आज मौसम अच्छा है और ~ हवा चल रही है।
opts.gu: આજે હવામાન સારું છે અને ~ પવન વાય છે.

opts.t: 言い訳を一切せず、彼は潔く全ての責任をとった。
opts.r: Iiwake o issai sezu, kare wa isagiyoku subete no sekinin o totta.
opts.en: Without a single excuse, he took full responsibility like a man. ✓
opts.hi: बिना कोई बहाना बनाए, उसने मर्दानगी से पूरी ज़िम्मेदारी ले ली।
opts.gu: કોઈ બહાનું કાઢ્યા વગર, તેણે ખેલદિલીથી બધી જવાબદારી લઈ લીધી.

opts.t: あらかじめ準備をしておいたので潔く会議が進む。
opts.r: Arakajime junbi o shite oita node isagiyoku kaigi ga susumu.
opts.en: We prepared in advance, so the meeting moves along ~.
opts.hi: पहले से तैयारी की थी, इसलिए बैठक ~ चल रही है।
opts.gu: અગાઉથી તૈયારી કરી હતી, એટલે મીટિંગ ~ ચાલે છે.

items.why: 潔い describes a person who accepts a loss, a mistake or a duty cleanly, with no excuses or clinging: 潔く負けを認める／諦める／責任をとる. The kanji 潔 also means "clean" (清潔), which is the trap in 1 and 2. 1 needs 清潔だ or きれいだ. 2 needs さわやかな or 清々しい ("refreshing"). 4 needs スムーズに or 順調に ("smoothly").

items.q: 手堅い
items.qr: tegatai — steady, safe, reliable (low risk)

opts.t: 長時間編み物をしていたので、手堅くなっている。
opts.r: Choujikan amimono o shite ita node, tegataku natte iru.
opts.en: I was knitting for a long time, so (my hands) have become ~.
opts.hi: बहुत देर तक बुनाई की, इसलिए (हाथ) ~ हो गए हैं।
opts.gu: લાંબો સમય ગૂંથણ કર્યું, એટલે (હાથ) ~ થઈ ગયા છે.

opts.t: 体調がよくないので、手堅く休むことにした。
opts.r: Taichou ga yoku nai node, tegataku yasumu koto ni shita.
opts.en: I don't feel well, so I decided to rest ~.
opts.hi: तबीयत ठीक नहीं है, इसलिए मैंने ~ आराम करने का फ़ैसला किया।
opts.gu: તબિયત સારી નથી, એટલે મેં ~ આરામ કરવાનું નક્કી કર્યું.

opts.t: 彼は手堅い仕事をしているだけあって、生活が派手になっている。
opts.r: Kare wa tegatai shigoto o shite iru dake atte, seikatsu ga hade ni natte iru.
opts.en: As you'd expect from someone with a ~ job, his lifestyle has become flashy.
opts.hi: ~ काम करने की वजह से ही उसकी ज़िंदगी शानो-शौक़त वाली हो गई है।
opts.gu: ~ કામ કરે છે એટલે જ તેનું જીવન ભપકાદાર થઈ ગયું છે.

opts.t: もうけは多くないが、手堅い商売をしている。
opts.r: Mouke wa ooku nai ga, tegatai shoubai o shite iru.
opts.en: The profits are not big, but he runs a steady, safe business. ✓
opts.hi: मुनाफ़ा ज़्यादा नहीं, पर वह सुरक्षित और भरोसेमंद व्यापार करता है।
opts.gu: નફો વધારે નથી, પણ તે સલામત અને ભરોસાપાત્ર ધંધો કરે છે.

items.why: 手堅い means "careful and safe, with little risk": 手堅い商売／投資／守備. The contrast "small profit, but steady" (もうけは多くないが) is its typical setting. 1 is about stiff hands, which needs 手がこわばって or 肩がこって; 手堅い is never physical. 2 needs 大事をとって ("to be on the safe side"). 3 is a logic clash: a steady, careful job does not lead to a flashy life; a job like 実入りのいい仕事 ("well-paid work") would fit.

items.q: つくづく
items.qr: tsukuzuku — deeply, thoroughly (feel or think)

opts.t: 久しぶりに故郷に戻ると、つくづく人が訪ねてきた。
opts.r: Hisashiburi ni kokyou ni modoru to, tsukuzuku hito ga tazunete kita.
opts.en: When I went back home after a long time, people came to visit ~.
opts.hi: बहुत दिनों बाद गाँव लौटा, तो लोग ~ मिलने आए।
opts.gu: ઘણા વખત પછી વતન પાછો ગયો, ત્યારે લોકો ~ મળવા આવ્યા.

opts.t: 毎日料理をしていたら、つくづく腕が上がってきた。
opts.r: Mainichi ryouri o shite itara, tsukuzuku ude ga agatte kita.
opts.en: Cooking every day, my skill has improved ~.
opts.hi: रोज़ खाना बनाते-बनाते मेरा हुनर ~ बढ़ गया।
opts.gu: રોજ રસોઈ બનાવતાં મારી આવડત ~ વધી ગઈ.

opts.t: 同じ失敗を繰り返す自分がつくづく嫌になる。
opts.r: Onaji shippai o kurikaesu jibun ga tsukuzuku iya ni naru.
opts.en: I get truly sick of myself for making the same mistake again and again. ✓
opts.hi: बार-बार एक ही ग़लती दोहराने वाले ख़ुद से मुझे सचमुच नफ़रत होने लगती है।
opts.gu: એક જ ભૂલ વારંવાર કરનાર મારી જાતથી મને ખરેખર કંટાળો આવે છે.

opts.t: 祖父は懐かしそうにつくづくと昔の話を語った。
opts.r: Sofu wa natsukashisou ni tsukuzuku to mukashi no hanashi o katatta.
opts.en: Grandfather told old stories ~, full of nostalgia.
opts.hi: दादाजी ने यादों में खोकर ~ पुरानी बातें सुनाईं।
opts.gu: દાદાએ યાદોમાં ખોવાઈને ~ જૂની વાતો કહી.

items.why: つくづく goes with verbs of feeling or realising: つくづく思う／感じる／嫌になる／感心する. It shows a feeling that comes from deep inside after thinking it over. 1 needs 次々と ("one after another"). 2 needs めきめき ("remarkably"): めきめき腕が上がる is a set phrase. 4 needs しみじみと ("with deep feeling"), which is close to つくづく but is the word used with 語る and 話す.

items.q: こってり
items.qr: kotteri — rich, heavy (taste); thoroughly, severely (scolded)

opts.t: カンニングが見つかり、先生にこってりと油を絞られた。
opts.r: Kanningu ga mitsukari, sensei ni kotteri to abura o shiborareta.
opts.en: I was caught cheating and got a real telling-off from the teacher. ✓
opts.hi: नकल करते पकड़ा गया, और टीचर से ख़ूब डाँट पड़ी।
opts.gu: ચોરી કરતાં પકડાયો, અને શિક્ષકે ખૂબ ઠપકો આપ્યો.

opts.t: 英才教育だと言い、子どもの頃からこってりピアノを練習させられた。
opts.r: Eisai kyouiku da to ii, kodomo no koro kara kotteri piano o renshuu saserareta.
opts.en: They called it gifted education and made me practise piano ~ from childhood.
opts.hi: इसे ख़ास शिक्षा बताकर बचपन से मुझसे ~ पियानो का अभ्यास कराया गया।
opts.gu: તેને ખાસ શિક્ષણ કહીને નાનપણથી મારી પાસે ~ પિયાનોનો અભ્યાસ કરાવાયો.

opts.t: この料理は脂肪が少なくこってりしていて、さわやかだ。
opts.r: Kono ryouri wa shibou ga sukunaku kotteri shite ite, sawayaka da.
opts.en: This dish is low in fat, ~ and refreshing.
opts.hi: इस व्यंजन में चर्बी कम है, यह ~ और ताज़गी-भरा है।
opts.gu: આ વાનગીમાં ચરબી ઓછી છે, તે ~ અને તાજગીભરી છે.

opts.t: 彼は相手の弱みをこってりとついてくる。
opts.r: Kare wa aite no yowami o kotteri to tsuite kuru.
opts.en: He attacks the other person's weak points ~.
opts.hi: वह सामने वाले की कमज़ोरी पर ~ वार करता है।
opts.gu: તે સામેવાળાની નબળાઈ પર ~ ઘા કરે છે.

items.why: こってり has two uses: a heavy, rich taste (こってりしたラーメン) and, figuratively, being scolded long and hard: こってり油を絞られる／しぼられる／叱られる. 1 is that idiom. 2 needs みっちり ("intensively, thoroughly", for training or practice). 3 is a contradiction: low fat and refreshing is あっさり, the opposite of こってり. 4 needs 容赦なく or しつこく ("mercilessly, persistently"); 弱みを突く does not take こってり.
